title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair
event_hint: AgenticDev 2026 study on correctness regression in agentic code repair loops
problem: Generate-test-revise loops in coding agents provide no reliability guarantee; correct patches can be destroyed in subsequent revisions, stale observations can revive old bugs, and correlated verifiers can confirm the same error
mechanism: State-bound typed revision contract that binds verifier evidence to exact code states, preserves verified checkpoints, and emits auditable admission receipts; separates admission, preservation, grounded certification, competence, and liveness

evidence.claim: Current correctness falls from 0.820 after one revision to 0.673 after two revisions
evidence.condition: Forced revision protocol, current traces, 30 HumanEval repairs, 900 three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Ever-correct rate rises to 0.847 despite current correctness decline
evidence.condition: Cumulative discovery metric, 30 HumanEval repairs, three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Stale traces harm 34/135 correct starts versus 4/135 with current traces, a 22.2-point increase
evidence.condition: 14B model replication, prespecified study, task-cluster 95% CI [8.9, 37.0], exact Holm p=0.0337
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, RQ2 discussion

evidence.claim: 16.0% of trajectories produce correct patch then lose it by revision 3
Reference implementation is executable specification, not evidence of improved repair competence
evidence.condition: Post-study implementation; not used to generate empirical results

evaluation_context: Sealed five-seed study over 30 HumanEval repairs producing 900 three-revision trajectories. Two common-state studies use 2,430 branches from identical frozen programs to remove post-treatment risk-set bias. Prespecified 14B replication with 135 starts per condition. Repository experiments over 24 bugs and four coder stacks (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct-AWQ, Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8, Devstral Small 2 24B). Reference implementation developed after empirical study completed.
limitations: Study scoped to HumanEval repair under forced-revision protocol; does not show adaptive loops must regress but demonstrates need for preservation and stopping rules. Repository experiments exposed floor effects and component heterogeneity without Holm-significant effects. Reference implementation is executable specification for contract enforcement, not evidence of improved repair competence or calibrated verifier dependence.
project_relevance: Relevant to agent acceleration project questions on whether parallel tool calls or caching introduce correctness risk. Demonstrates that stale feedback harms correct starts (22.2-point increase in harm). State-bound evidence binding suggests approach for ensuring tool-call reuse and read results are tied to exact code states. However, limited to code repair domain; direct applicability to read/grep acceleration unclear.
